metadata.notes: Webhook payload shape: { event, source, version, timestamp, userId, data: { supplierCount, userEmail, userName, month, suppliers: [{ name, tier }] } }

mapper.name: scorecardHtml
mapper.value:
{{"

Monthly Supplier Scorecard — " + ifempty(1.body.data.month; formatDate(now; 'MMMM YYYY')) + "

Hi " + ifempty(1.body.data.userName; 'there') + ", here is your supplier scorecard for " + ifempty(1.body.data.month; formatDate(now; 'MMMM YYYY')) + ".

" + join(map(1.body.data.suppliers; ""); "") + "
SupplierTier
" + item.name + "" + item.tier + "

→ View full scorecard in ISC

"}}

metadata.notes: Builds the HTML table directly from the webhook payload's suppliers array (1.body.data.suppliers). Each entry has 'name' and 'tier'. Replace YOUR_ISC_DOMAIN.
Sends to 1.body.data.userEmail. No ISC API key needed — all data comes from the webhook payload. Replace YOUR_ISC_DOMAIN.

setupSteps: 1. In Make.com, create a new scenario and import this JSON (three dots → Import Blueprint).
2. Click the Webhook module and copy the generated webhook URL.
3. In ISC → Admin → Integration Hub → Webhooks, create a webhook with event 'schedule.monthly_scorecard' and paste that URL.
4. Add your Gmail connection to the Gmail module.
5. Replace YOUR_ISC_DOMAIN in the Set Variable module and in the Gmail 'from' address.
6. The supplier data (name, tier), user email, user name, and month all come from the ISC webhook payload — no ISC API key needed.
7. ISC fires this on the 1st of each month automatically — no Make.com schedule trigger needed.
